extracted.intended_audience: federal executive departments and agencies (agency officials responsible for regulatory policy and implementation); interested State, local, and tribal governments
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for executive branch agencies implementing Executive Order 12875 to reduce unfunded mandates, improve consultation with state/local/tribal governments, and streamline waiver processes. Covers applicability, agency responsibilities, timelines for waiver decisions, and legal effect.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reduction of Unfunded Mandates (general prohibition)
rubrics_metrics.description: To the extent feasible and permitted by law, no executive department or agency shall promulgate any regulation that is not required by statute and that creates a mandate upon a State, local, or tribal government, unless one of the specified exceptions applies.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Purpose: reduce imposition of unfunded mandates upon State, local, and tribal governments and avoid excessive micromanagement and unnecessary regulation. This is a prescriptive constraint on agency rulemaking subject to feasibility and legal limits.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exception — Federal funding for direct costs
rubrics_metrics.description: An agency may promulgate a regulation that creates a mandate on State, local, or tribal governments only if funds necessary to pay the direct costs incurred by those governments in complying with the mandate are provided by the Federal Government.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is one of two explicit exceptions to the general prohibition on unfunded mandates; agencies must ensure direct cost funding is provided before issuing such mandates when relying on this exception.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exception — Prior consultation documentation to OMB
rubrics_metrics.description: An agency may promulgate a regulation creating a mandate if, prior to formal promulgation of the regulation, the agency provides to the Director of the Office of Management and Budget a description of the extent of the agency's prior consultation with representatives of affected State, local, and tribal governments, the nature of their concerns, any written communications submitted to the agency by such units of government, and the agency's position supporting the need to issue the regulation containing the mandate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This exception requires agencies to document consultation efforts and provide OMB a narrative of consultations, concerns raised, written submissions, and the agency’s justification for the regulation before finalizing rules that impose mandates.

rubrics_metrics.name: Requirement to develop meaningful consultation processes
rubrics_metrics.description: Each agency shall develop an effective process to permit elected officials and other representatives of State, local, and tribal governments to provide meaningful and timely input in the development of regulatory proposals containing significant unfunded mandates.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Agencies must create procedures enabling timely, substantive input from intergovernmental representatives during regulatory development; the order emphasizes both meaningfulness and timeliness of input as standards of the process.

rubrics_metrics.name: Streamline waiver application processes
rubrics_metrics.description: Each agency shall review its waiver application process and take appropriate steps to streamline that process.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Agencies are directed to assess and improve internal procedures to make waiver applications easier to submit and process; this is an administrative-improvement obligation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consider waivers to increase flexible policy approaches
rubrics_metrics.description: Each agency shall, to the extent practicable and permitted by law, consider any application by a State, local, or tribal government for a waiver of statutory or regulatory requirements with a general view toward increasing opportunities for utilizing flexible policy approaches at the State, local, and tribal level where the proposed waiver is consistent with applicable Federal policy objectives and is otherwise appropriate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Substantive standard for waiver adjudication: agencies should favor flexibility when waivers align with federal policy objectives and are appropriate. This sets a policy-driven evaluative lens for waiver decisions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Timely decision and notice on complete waiver applications
rubrics_metrics.description: Each agency shall, to the fullest extent practicable and permitted by law, render a decision upon a complete application for a waiver within 120 days of receipt. If the application for a waiver is not granted, the agency shall provide the applicant with timely written notice of the decision and the reasons therefor.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Operational deadline and notice requirement: agencies are expected to decide complete waiver requests within 120 days and to provide written reasons if denying a waiver. Applies only to discretionary statutory or regulatory requirements subject to waiver.

rubrics_metrics.name: Limitation — applies only to discretionary, waivable requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: The section on waivers applies only to statutory or regulatory requirements of programs that are discretionary and subject to waiver by the agency.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Clarifies scope of waiver obligations: mandatory or non-waivable provisions are not covered by the waiver-timing and consideration directives.

rubrics_metrics.name: Responsibility for agency implementation
rubrics_metrics.description: The Chief Operating Officer of each agency shall be responsible for ensuring the implementation of and compliance with this order.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Designates responsibility within agencies: the named COO (or equivalent) is accountable for implementing the order’s requirements and ensuring agency compliance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Relationship to Executive Order 12866
rubrics_metrics.description: This order shall supplement but not supersede the requirements contained in Executive Order No. 12866 ('Regulatory Planning and Review').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Directs agencies to apply this order alongside existing EO 12866 obligations; where both apply, EO 12866 remains effective and is not overridden by this order.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scope and applicability (definition of 'executive agency' and independent agencies)
rubrics_metrics.description: Executive agency means any authority of the United States that is an 'agency' under 44 U.S.C. 3502(1), other than those considered to be independent regulatory agencies as defined in 44 U.S.C. 3502(10). Independent agencies are requested to comply with the provisions of this order.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Defines which entities are bound versus requested to comply: cabinet-level and other executive branch agencies are covered; independent regulatory agencies are not required but are asked to follow the order.

rubrics_metrics.name: Judicial review / legal effect
rubrics_metrics.description: This order is intended only to improve the internal management of the executive branch and is not intended to, and does not, create any right or benefit, substantive or procedural, enforceable at law or equity by a party against the United States, its agencies or instrumentalities, its officers or employees, or any other person.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: States the order is not meant to create private enforceable rights; it is an internal management directive and not a source of legal claims.

rubrics_metrics.name: Effective date
rubrics_metrics.description: This order shall be effective 90 days after the date of this order.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Sets the operative start date for the order’s requirements (90 days post-signing).
